proof_summary: Assuming either prime family is finite, bound it by \(N\) and apply the decomposition hypothesis to \((N+4)!/6\), obtaining \((N+4)!=(6x-1)+(6y+1)\). The bounded relevant prime (or its twin partner) divides the factorial, hence divides the other prime summand; primality forces equality, contradicting that the two summands are respectively \(-1\) and \(+1\pmod 6\).
